title: Interest Rate Futures: Day Counts, Bond Futures, and the Wild Card
targetAudiencePersona: Fixed Income Portfolio Manager & Futures Basis Trader
prerequisites: Bond pricing, yield to maturity, and coupon discounting from Chapter 4
Concept of short selling and delivery obligations
Cost of carry and forward pricing parity from Chapter 5
learningOutcomes: Differentiate between Actual/Actual, 30/360, and Actual/360 day count conventions.
Calculate dirty cash price from quoted clean price and accrued interest.
Understand CBOT/CME Treasury bond futures specifications and 32nds price quoting.
Apply Conversion Factors (CF) to compute exact invoice cash received upon delivery.
Identify the Cheapest-to-Deliver (CTD) bond using Cost = Spot - (Futures * CF).
Explain the mechanics of the Wild Card Play and why delivery options lower futures prices.

sections.title: Day Counts & The Clean vs Dirty Price Paradox
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Explain how day count conventions govern accrued interest and why invoice cash differs from screen quotes.
keyPoints: Treasury bonds use Actual/Actual in period; corporates use 30/360; money market uses Actual/360.
Clean price excludes accrued interest; dirty cash price is actual invoice settlement: Cash = Clean + AI.
Accrued interest drops to zero immediately after coupon dates, creating the sawtooth price chart.
sections.formulaUsed: Cash Price = Quoted Price + Accrued Interest

sections.title: Treasury Bond Futures & Conversion Factors
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Formulate contract specifications, 32nds quotation, and the 6% conversion factor standardization.
keyPoints: Contract allows delivery of any Treasury bond maturing in 15 to 25 years.
Conversion factor equals the price of $1 par to yield 6.0% semiannual.
Invoice cash received by short party: (Futures Price * CF) + Accrued Interest.

sections.title: The Cheapest-to-Deliver (CTD) Bond
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Derive Cost to Deliver = Spot - (Futures * CF) and demonstrate CTD selection across 3 bonds.
keyPoints: Short seller minimizes delivery cost: Cost = Spot - (Futures * CF).
The bond with the lowest delivery cost is selected as CTD.
Futures price tracks the CTD bond closely throughout the life of the contract.

sections.title: Yield Regimes and CTD Selection Rules
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Establish heuristics governing CTD choice when market yields trade above or below 6%.
keyPoints: When market yields > 6%: CF system favors long-maturity, low-coupon bonds.
When market yields < 6%: CF system favors short-maturity, high-coupon bonds.
Upward sloping yield curves favor long-maturity bonds.

sections.title: The Wild Card Play & Embedded Delivery Options
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Dissect Snapshot 6.2 to analyze the 2:00 PM to 8:00 PM delivery timing window.
keyPoints: Futures settle at 2:00 PM Chicago time, but delivery notice can be submitted until 8:00 PM.
Late afternoon bond price drops allow short sellers to buy cheap spot and deliver at high 2:00 PM price.
This embedded timing option lowers the futures price below theoretical parity.

misconceptions.misconception: The bond buyer pays the exact quoted price displayed on financial market screens.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Screen quotes show clean prices. The buyer must pay the dirty cash price, which adds accrued interest earned by the seller since the last coupon.

misconceptions.misconception: Treasury bond futures require delivery of a specific unique benchmark government bond.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: The contract allows delivery of any US Treasury bond maturing in 15 to 25 years, standardized via conversion factors.

misconceptions.misconception: The short seller delivers whichever bond has the lowest spot market price.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: The short seller delivers the bond that minimizes Cost = Spot - (Futures * CF). A higher-priced bond with a high conversion factor can be cheaper to deliver.

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: A Treasury bond futures price is quoted at 93.00. Bond A has spot price $99.50 and conversion factor 1.0382. Bond B has spot price $143.50 and conversion factor 1.5188. An analyst calculates the delivery cost.
activeRecallQuiz.question: Which bond is cheaper to deliver and what is its net cost?

coreTakeaways: Day counts (Actual/Actual vs 30/360) determine accrued interest and dirty cash invoice settlement.
Conversion factors (CF) normalize eligible Treasury bonds to a 6.0% semiannual yield standard.
The short seller delivers the Cheapest-to-Deliver (CTD) bond minimizing Cost = Spot - (Futures * CF).
When yields exceed 6%, long-maturity low-coupon bonds become CTD; below 6%, short-maturity high-coupon bonds win.
The Wild Card Play grants short sellers a 6-hour delivery option after 2:00 PM, reducing futures prices.
